questions.q: What does RBAC assign, and at what scope?
options: Broad roles (like Storage Blob Data Reader/Contributor/Owner) to an identity, at a scope you choose — subscription, resource group, account, or container
Individual read/write/execute permissions on a single file only
Passwords for each user accessing the storage account
Network firewall rules only
questions.explain: RBAC is Azure's general-purpose, scope-based role assignment system.

questions.q: What are ACLs, and why do they only exist on ADLS Gen2?
options: POSIX-style read/write/execute permissions on individual directories and files — possible only because hierarchical namespace gives real directory objects to attach them to
ACLs are identical to RBAC roles, just with a different name
ACLs exist on plain Blob storage too, with no difference
ACLs are a billing feature unrelated to permissions
questions.explain: Plain Blob storage has no real directories, so there's nothing for an ACL to attach to.

questions.q: In what order does Azure check RBAC and ACLs for a request?
options: RBAC (and ABAC conditions) first — ACLs are only checked if RBAC doesn't already grant access
ACLs first, then RBAC only if ACLs deny access
Both are checked simultaneously with no defined order
Only one system is ever active at a time, never both
questions.explain: This is the real, official flow: RBAC/ABAC is checked first, and ACLs are the fallback check.

questions.q: If an identity already holds the Storage Blob Data Owner RBAC role, does the ACL check still run?
options: No — an RBAC role like Owner or Contributor grants access immediately, and the ACL check never runs
Yes, ACLs are always checked regardless of RBAC role
Only on weekends
Only if the identity is a service principal
questions.explain: The ACL check is a fallback for identities that don't already have a sufficient RBAC role.

questions.q: Why do real production data lakes typically use both RBAC and ACLs together?
options: RBAC is coarse but easy to manage for broad team access; ACLs are granular but require directory-by-directory maintenance, useful for genuine exceptions
Because Azure requires both to be configured before any access is possible
ACLs replace RBAC entirely in modern Azure deployments
RBAC only works for read operations, never writes
questions.explain: RBAC handles broad access efficiently; ACLs handle the fine-grained exceptions RBAC alone can't express.
